header.running_head: The Hijrah of Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)

blocks.text: Rasulullaah ﷺ then called for the two orphans to buy the land so that a Masjid could be built on it. They said, "(Instead of selling the land) We would rather give it to you as a gift, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" Rasulullaah ﷺ refused to accept it from them as a gift until they he was able to buy it from them. Rasulullaah ﷺ then had the site fixed for a Masjid. Rasulullaah ﷺ himself carried the unbaked bricks for the Masjid with the Sahabah (RA). As he carried the bricks he sang:

blocks.arabic_text:
هٰذَا الْحِمَالُ لَا حِمَالُ خَيْبَرْ
هٰذَا أَبَرُّ رَبَّنَا وَأَطْهَرْ
blocks.text:
"Lifting these bricks is not like lifting the dates and grapes of Khaybar
O our Rabb! This is more virtuous and purer"
Another couplet Rasulullaah ﷺ would recite was:

blocks.arabic_text:
اَللّٰهُمَّ إِنَّ الْأَجْرَ أَجْرُ الْآخِرَهْ
فَارْحَمِ الْأَنْصَارَ وَالْمُهَاجِرَهْ
blocks.text:
O Allaah! The true rewards are those of the Aakhirah
So do shower Your mercy on the Ansaar and Muhaajirah (Muhaajireen)

The narrator says that Rasulullaah ﷺ also recited the poem of a Muslim whose name he was not told. Ibn Shihaab (RA) says, "Besides these couplets, no Hadith has reached us in which Rasulullaah ﷺ has recited a complete poem." [^1]

Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) says, "I was one of the children running as the people said, 'Muhammad ﷺ has arrived!' I ran on but could not see anything. When the people again called, 'Muhammad ﷺ has arrived!' I ran again but could still not see anything. Rasulullaah ﷺ and his companion Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) eventually arrived and sat down in an uninhabited area of Madinah. They then sent a Bedouin to announce to the Ansaar that they had arrived. Consequently, approximately five hundred of the Ansaar came out to welcome them. When the Ansaar came, they said, 'Come along. You are both safe and will be obeyed.' Rasulullaah ﷺ and his companion walked amongst us and the people of Madinah all came out to welcome them. In fact, even the young girls stood above the houses vying with each other to look as they asked, 'Which of them is Rasulullaah ﷺ? Which of them is Rasulullaah ﷺ?' We had never seen a sight like this."
Hadhrat Anas (RA) also said, "I have seen Rasulullaah ﷺ the day he arrived in Madinah and the day he passed away and have never seen any days like them." [^2]
Hadhrat Aa'isha narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, the women and children sang:

blocks.arabic_text:
طَلَعَ الْبَدْرُ عَلَيْنَا مِنْ ثَنِيَّاتِ الْوَدَاعِ
وَجَبَ الشُّكْرُ عَلَيْنَا مَا دَعَا لِلّٰهِ دَاعٍ
blocks.text: "The full moon has risen above us from the Valley of Wadaa
Bukhari as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.3 Pg.186).
Ahmad and Bayhaqi as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.3 Pg.197).
